body:
The #590 refutation identified G-03 Low: the Steam runtime transaction is the only embedded Python helper invoked as python3 - after loading the profile. The other helpers use /usr/bin/python3 -I -S -B -. Current-directory/site/PYTHONPATH shadowing can change the runtime helper imports; absence of shipped PYTHON settings does not close that gap.

User direction: “Let's fix any gaps we discover before we generate a new build.”

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: the exact invocation and embedded stdlib imports can run against a harmless synthetic poisoned module in a disposable guest. No network, actual Steam download, account, or device needed.

- [x] Source/history confirms no intended site dependency and the single invocation uses the same isolated interpreter flags as the other helpers.
- [x] A bounded VM negative/positive control records original exits and proves profile/current-directory import poisoning affects the old invocation but not the corrected invocation.
- [ ] Independent source review and affected installed/source identity are included in the next candidate qualification, without repeating the full Steam transaction matrix.

The global client360-second budget lead remains an explicitly documented timing-risk observation, not a confirmed defect or reason to silently weaken deadlines.

Verified October15: source d9054efc46 (published feature branch47dda767), independently reviewed exact one-line invocation delta. Controls02 original runtime/export/launcher/monitor0; baseline function1 with harmless import shadow reached, isolated candidate0 with complete synthetic runtime transaction, identical embedded body, no timeout or remaining process group. Evidence: docs/qa-logs/2026-10-15-audit-followup-controls/ (prepared for publication). Installed Python is used; transports/library bytes are explicit fixtures, no native ARM/client claim. Final changed-image identity remains the last open criterion.
